source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
1. Enter BMC-Web -> Click tab "Settings" -> Click "User Management" to view user accounts.    
2. Click the user account which needs to be deleted.
3. Delete an user.

    【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The user can be removed successfully.
2. User list will not show this user again.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl + jq (Web UI action by operator)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Delete user account - WebUI is driven through the BMC Web UI by the operator (add/delete/modify a user + set privileges). Agent verifies the resulting account list: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts 2>&1 | jq ".Members[]?|{Id,UserName,RoleId}" 2>/dev/null after the operator acts.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish account-list JSON after the WebUI delete user account so the user confirms the account was added/deleted/modified as expected.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: account add/delete/modify is a security-sensitive write done in the Web UI by the operator; agent only reads the resulting list.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes the operator-driven security write but conflates add/delete/modify, uses insecure partial readback and does not identify the immutable target, exclude protected accounts, define delete-versus-disable/session semantics, verify authentication denial or provide recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires one disposable account, immutable ID/username correlation, complete account/session baseline, independent recovery, one approved WebUI deletion, full post-state/audit, denied login/session behavior and unrelated-account continuity.

historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding Add row may create a disposable target, but this Delete row independently requires unique identity and removal/authentication evidence. The next Modify row must not be combined.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI removes one exact approved disposable user so it disappears from supported inventories and can no longer authenticate, while protected accounts, unrelated users, roles and recovery access remain intact.
original_method: Correlate one disposable username to immutable slot/ID across complete WebUI/API inventory; preserve account/role/session baseline and independent recovery; define delete-versus-disable and session expectations; delete the exact account once after approval; capture UI/audit and complete post-state; verify denied new login and approved session invalidation; confirm unrelated/local-admin access; restore only if explicitly required.
manual_activity: An owner classifies the exact account as disposable, approves delete-versus-disable and session/final-state expectations, verifies independent recovery and authorizes one WebUI action. A human operates and visually confirms the source WebUI. Automation may collect complete redacted inventory, audit and bounded login evidence but cannot choose the target or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: Exact disposable username plus immutable account slot/ID and role
Complete account/role/session baseline and active-session policy
Expected login denial/session invalidation and unrelated access
Independent recovery and approved final/restore state
safety_requirements: Do not select by ambiguous display name, delete protected/default/recovery/directory accounts, bulk-delete users or expose passwords/tokens in evidence.
Verify immutable target identity, role, current sessions, complete baseline and independent recovery before the WebUI delete; do not clear security logs.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one exact account only. Do not retry on timeout, terminate the recovery session or touch a second account.
Do not use `curl -k`, a disappearing UI row or HTTP status as sole proof; collect complete trusted post-inventory and audit state.
Verify denied new authentication and defined existing-session behavior separately while confirming unrelated/local-admin access.
Stop on wrong/partial target, unexpected unrelated change, continued login, recovery failure or cleanup ambiguity; use independent recovery and approved restore without bulk recreation.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target identity, protected exclusions, baseline, session/delete semantics, recovery and final state; present one WebUI delete for approval.
After approval, guide/capture the exact WebUI delete once and collect redacted UI/audit plus complete paginated account/session readback.
Test deleted-account login denial and expected session behavior while confirming unrelated and local-admin continuity.
Restore only if explicitly approved, reconcile baseline, archive evidence and stop without another account action, retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the immutable disposable target, delete/disable semantics, session behavior, final state and protected exclusions.
Approve one WebUI deletion, bounded denial test, independent recovery and any exact restore.
Review state/auth/session/audit/recovery evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The API list is relevant corroboration but `-k`, inline credentials, partial fields and no pagination are unsafe/incomplete. Generic add/delete/modify wording does not prove the exact delete target, authentication denial or session behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact source WebUI delete for one immutable approved account, then trusted complete account/session/audit readback and bounded denial checks; never substitute an API delete without approved coverage mapping.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Settings > User Management path, selection/delete steps, removal/disappearance Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek proposal/risk and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Delete one immutable disposable account through the WebUI after recovery gating, then prove complete state removal/disable semantics, authentication denial, session behavior and unrelated access.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC WebUI User Management page and account/session services.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, WebUI build, account/session schema and browser/client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor account delete/disable/session specification and Project access-control/recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds immutable identity, protected exclusions, session/auth checks, complete readback and recovery while retaining the WebUI action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: API deletion does not prove WebUI control; row disappearance does not prove authentication denial; disable is not identical to deletion unless Project accepts it.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Disposable ID, baseline, session semantics, recovery, denial and final state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-user deletion can remove recovery; active sessions may survive; cached UI data can falsely show removal.

project_override_considerations: Browser automation or vendor API may be approved only when the original WebUI method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, exact delete/disable/session equivalence and uncovered visual/UI coverage are recorded. Read-only listing is not an equivalent override.
expected_evidence: Approved BMC/firmware/WebUI target, immutable disposable account identity, protected exclusions, complete redacted account/role/session baseline and recovery proof
One WebUI delete/disable screenshot/DOM and audit event tied to the immutable target
Complete trusted post-account/session inventory proving only the target changed and documenting delete versus disable state
Deleted credential denial, expected existing-session behavior and unrelated/local-admin continuity
Approved final/restore state, preserved logs/no secret exposure/no retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require deleting one WebUI user and removing it from the list. Platform delete-versus-disable/session details are Project readiness inputs rather than competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The account-removal objective is explicit. A disposable target, session semantics and recovery can be supplied, so execution is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but isolates Delete from other actions, replaces insecure partial list evidence with immutable target, complete state, denial/session and recovery proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its critical controls and sharpens exact WebUI coverage, delete-versus-disable result and no-retry boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic post-list confirmation with one-target state/auth/session verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Uses Add only as a possible disposable setup and keeps Modify separate; neither substitutes for deletion evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents deletion of the wrong or recovery account and prevents a hidden UI row from being reported as removal without authentication/session proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: Account deletion affects identity, authorization and sessions. A UI row can disappear because of filtering or caching, while the account may remain enabled or an active session may persist. Evidence must bind one immutable disposable ID to a single WebUI action, complete post-state and denied authentication, with unrelated recovery access verified throughout.
